title: Novel pneumonie risque score (PRS)
formula:
The probability of radiographic pneumonia is calculated based on the following inputs:

- Age, years
- Fever ***** at home or in ED (yes or no)
- First O2 saturation obtained
- Crackles (yes or no)
- Wheezing (yes or no)

% risk of radiographic pneumonia = e^x^/(1+e^x^)*100

where x = 18.05624 + 0.098308*(Age, years) + 1.144985*(Fever) - 0.21636*(First O2 saturation obtained) + 0.407494*(Crackles) - 0.907087*(Wheezing)

Pneumonia Risk Score (PRS):

| % Risk of Radiographic Pneumonia | Pneumonia Risk Score (PRS) |
| --- | --- |
| <5% (low) | 1 |
| ≥5% and <11% (low) | 2 |
| ≥11% and <21% (medium) | 3 |
| ≥21% and <51% (medium) | 4 |
| ≥51% and <75% (high) | 5 |
| ≥75% (high) | 6 |

***** A fever is defined as >38°C (>100.4°F).

how_to_use.when: Do you use the Novel Pneumonia Risk Score (PRS) and want to contribute your expertise?[Join](https://www.mdcalc.com/join-us)our contributor team!

next_steps.advice:
| Pneumonia Risk Score | Recommendations |
| --- | --- |
| 1-2 | Low risk, consider deferring chest X-ray and antibiotics |
| 3-4 | Moderate risk, consider chest X-ray to further evaluate for pneumonia |
| 5-6 | High risk, consider chest X-ray vs. empiric antibiotics |

*Scores were derived from a population of children presenting to an emergency department in whom a clinician obtained a CXR for suspicion for pneumonia. This score may over-estimate actual risk when applied to children with lower suspicion of pneumonia.
